decisions.rationale: 'FMR1 deficiency' names a specific genetic deficiency state (the FMR1 loss-of-function condition). Like 'C7 deficiency', the qualifier makes it a specific disease rather than the excluded general term 'deficiency' alone.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms); Examples 6

decisions.rationale: 'Fragile X syndrome' is a single, well-defined genetic disease with one specific definition, so it is a Specific Disease.
'mental retardation' here refers to a broad family of conditions with many causes (Fragile X is described as one common cause of it), so it is a grey-area term best treated as a Disease Class.

'macroorchidism' is a specific, clinically defined condition (enlarged testes) described as a phenotype of the disease model. It has a single definition and is not a general term, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
'behavioral abnormalities' is a vague phenotype description built around the very general term 'abnormalities', which the guidelines explicitly exclude.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms such as 'abnormalities')

decisions.rationale: 'fragile X syndrome' refers to a single specific disease, identical in meaning to the other occurrences, and is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: 'Macro-orchidism' is the same specific condition as 'macroorchidism' (enlarged testes) in a different spelling, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: In 'complex behavioral phenotype in fragile X patients', 'fragile X' is a disease name used as a noun modifier of 'patients', not a standalone disease mention. It is therefore annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: 'fragile X syndrome' in 'gene therapy for fragile X syndrome' is a full, specific disease name and is annotated as a Specific Disease.
